name: Insurance agencies and brokers

problems.words: Renewals slip through and we only find out after the policy has lapsed
quick_ideas: Pull every renewal date into one shared list with a named owner per policy, so no renewal belongs to nobody
Hold one short Monday huddle to hand out the coming month's renewals, so calls start before the due date, not after.

workzap_build.text: customer_messaging — A renewal register that reminds the owning agent ahead of each due date every day, sends the customer a renewal reminder on WhatsApp with their permission, and shows the owner which renewals were saved or lost by line and agent.

problems.ask_first: Roughly how many renewals come up in a normal month?
problems.free_stops: The reminder timings, the register layout and the customer message wording go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count last month's lapsed renewals and note who noticed each one first, so you can see where the handoff is failing.
Give one person the daily renewal due check at a fixed time, so missed dates stop surfacing only after lapse.

problems.words: Renewal dates live in three Excel sheets and nobody owns the list
quick_ideas: Pick one master list and freeze the other sheets as read-only, so there is a single version of the truth
Decide one person who is accountable for the list being complete, so gaps have an owner.

workzap_build.text: Renewals, leads, quotes and claims would sit in one place under the agency's own account, with access by role, updated as staff work rather than copied between sheets.

problems.ask_first: Are the sheets split by agent, by line or by insurer?
problems.free_stops: How the sheets are merged and which fields matter for each line is detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare the renewal dates for the same few files across all sheets, so you can see how often the lists disagree.
Keep one notebook beside the main desk for every renewal date change, so sheet updates come from one place each day.

problems.words: Facebook and WhatsApp leads come in and nobody calls them back in time
quick_ideas: Send every ad form and enquiry to one shared business number instead of personal phones, so leads stop disappearing
Agree a same-day first-reply rule for every enquiry, because customers tend to go with whoever answers first.

workzap_build.text: One lead inbox that pulls in WhatsApp, website and ad-form enquiries, assigns each to a producer, times the first response and nudges when a lead sits untouched.

problems.ask_first: Where do most of your new enquiries come from?
problems.free_stops: Assignment rules, response timers and follow-up sequences are set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note today's enquiry time and first callback time for each lead, so you can see how long replies really take.
Give one person each shift the callback list and handover, so new enquiries are owned the moment they arrive.

problems.words: Getting quotes from four insurers takes days of emailing and chasing
quick_ideas: Send each quote request to all chosen insurers at the same moment, so the slowest one sets the pace instead of the sum of all
Keep one line per request showing who has replied, so chasing is targeted rather than guessed.

workzap_build.text: A quote request tracker that records which insurers were asked, chases the ones that have not replied, and shows average reply time per insurer each month.

problems.ask_first: What part of getting a quote takes the longest?
problems.free_stops: The request format and chasing schedule are worked out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note when each quote request was sent and when each reply arrived, so the slowest chasers stand out by insurer.
Set one fixed chasing time daily for outstanding quote requests, so follow up happens before the inbox gets buried.

problems.words: We spend on ads but cannot say which ones produced policies
quick_ideas: Ask every new enquiry where they heard about you and note it, so each policy has a source
Give each ad its own contact link or number, so enquiries separate themselves by campaign.

workzap_build.text: dashboards_reports — Codes and links per ad that follow each enquiry through to a written policy, with a monthly view of enquiries and policies by source.

problems.ask_first: Do most of your ads bring phone calls, or WhatsApp messages?
problems.free_stops: How codes are set up per channel and tied to policies is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count this week's new enquiries by where they said they found you, so policy sources stop being guesswork.
Give one staff member the job of noting enquiry source on every new case, so each sale can be traced back later.

problems.words: Insurer commission does not match what we expected and reconciling takes weeks
quick_ideas: Note the expected commission at the time each policy is written, so there is something to check the statement against
List mismatches per insurer and raise them in one go, so gaps are chased as a batch; talk to your accountant about how to record them.

workzap_build.text: An expected-versus-received commission ledger by insurer and month that highlights every mismatch immediately and keeps a running list of what is still owed.

problems.ask_first: Is it the amount or the timing of commission that causes more trouble?
problems.free_stops: The matching logic and ledger structure are covered in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note how many statement line items needed manual checking last cycle, so you can see where reconciliation effort is piling up.
Give one person a fixed weekly slot to collect all mismatch notes in one notebook, so follow ups stop getting scattered.

problems.words: Sub-agents argue over who brought which customer and what share they are owed
quick_ideas: Write the credit rule on one page and get every sub-agent to agree to it, so disputes are settled by the rule, not by memory
Record who introduced a customer at the first enquiry, not at the sale, so credit is fixed early.

workzap_build.text: A producer and sub-agent credit log that applies the agreed share rule to each policy and sends every sub-agent a monthly statement.

problems.ask_first: Do the arguments come mostly over who introduced the customer, or over the share owed?
problems.free_stops: How the share rules are encoded and statements produced is in the solution document; pi does not decide who is right in any dispute.

extra_ideas.text: Note how many recent sales had more than one sub-agent claiming credit, so you can see how often the rule is tested.
Make one person write the introducer on the shared case list when the enquiry arrives, so payout arguments have an early record.

problems.words: Claims follow-up is all on WhatsApp and customers keep asking for updates we do not have
quick_ideas: Keep one claims list with stage, next action and owner per case, so updates come from one place
Give every open claim a fixed update day, so customers hear from you before they chase.

workzap_build.text: A claims follow-up tracker with stages, owners and next actions that reminds staff when an update is due and shows the owner which claims are stuck.

problems.ask_first: Where do the documents for one claim usually end up?
problems.free_stops: The stage list, update rhythm and customer wording go in the solution document; pi never comments on claim outcomes.

extra_ideas.text: Count open claims with no recorded next action today, so you can see why update requests keep piling up.
Give one staff member a fixed afternoon claims roundup, so customers get updates from the latest office view.

problems.words: Corporate clients send group medical additions and deletions by email and we miss some
quick_ideas: Ask each corporate client to send changes in one fixed format to one address, so nothing arrives in a side thread
Confirm every change back once the insurer accepts it, so both sides know it is done.

workzap_build.text: A change-request log per corporate client that tracks each addition or deletion to confirmation and flags any still open.

problems.ask_first: Do the missed additions and deletions come from a few corporate clients, or from many?
problems.free_stops: The request format and confirmation steps are detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare a few client change emails against what was actually sent on, so missed additions and deletions show up clearly.
Make one person maintain a single pending changes page for each corporate account, so requests stop getting lost across threads.

problems.words: No single view of how many policies we wrote this month by line
quick_ideas: Pick the four or five numbers you actually want each month (policies by line, renewals due and lost, leads) so reporting has a target
Count them by hand once this month, so you see where the data is missing.

workzap_build.text: An owner screen showing policies written, renewals due and lost, leads and response times by branch and producer, refreshed daily.

problems.ask_first: Which lines matter most to see: health, motor, life or something else?
problems.free_stops: Which figures feed the screen and how they are pulled together is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count policies written this month by each line on one notebook page, so you can see which line lacks daily visibility.
Make one staff member update a single monthly page by line each afternoon, so month end totals are ready without chasing.

problems.words: An agent left and took the client list with them
quick_ideas: Move client contact to business numbers and accounts the agency owns, so relationships stay with the firm
Ask your lawyer what your staff agreements should say about client records.

workzap_build.text: Client, renewal and claims records would be held under the agency's own account, with access by role that could be switched off the day someone leaves.

problems.ask_first: Did the agent keep clients' numbers on his own phone, or in the agency's files?
problems.free_stops: Access roles and handover steps are set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many active client conversations are still only on ex-staff contacts or notebooks, so the handover risk becomes visible.
Give one staff member a weekly check of where new client contacts are saved, so records stay under the agency’s control.

never_say: Which insurer, policy, premium or level of cover a customer should take, or whether they "need" cover.
Whether a claim will be paid, is genuine, or how policy wording or exclusions should be read.
Anything on SECP, UAE Insurance Authority or Canadian provincial regulator requirements; point to their compliance adviser or lawyer.
Anything that helps backdate policies, inflate claims, alter documents or split invoices.
Any request for policy numbers, customer names, IDs, medical details, vehicle numbers or bank details.

sample_reply.person: Bhai renewals ka koi sahi tareeqah nahi, har agent apni Excel chalata hai aur policies lapse ho jati hain. Koi hal batao.
sample_reply.pi:
Haan, is par kaam ho sakta hai, aur pehla qadam aasan hai.
Pehle, saari renewal dates ek hi list mein le aayein aur har policy ke saath ek zimmedar ka naam likhein, taake koi renewal be-malik na rahe.
Doosra, har Monday chhoti si meeting mein agle mahine ki renewals baant dein, taake call due date se pehle ho.
Workzap ye tayyar kar sakta hai: har agent ko waqt pe yaad-dehani, customer ko unki ijazat se WhatsApp reminder, aur aap ke saamne roz ki report ke kaun si renewal bachi aur kaun si lapse hui.
